limitations: syntax modernization: only proven-safe error checks, simple value choices, nil guards/defaults and contextually typed function literals are suggested; arbitrary equivalent control flow is not recognized

database/sql ScanStruct/Collect/CollectOne: mapping is strict (unmapped, ambiguous or duplicate columns are errors), tag comma options are reserved errors, RawBytes fields and element types are rejected; native pgx outside database/sql is not covered
parameter-label API inventory currently records darwin/arm64; other platform inventories remain unrecorded while additional platform validation is deferred
! and one-line or require the nearest function to return exactly error last, including in _test.go; tests use explicit block handlers for Fatal
source inliner: Gon control-flow callee bodies and affected call sites are deliberately declined
extract variable: lazy branches and whole conditional expressions are deliberately declined
cgo: existing restriction on error propagation inside pointer-check rewritten C-call arguments still applies
source inliner: Gon control-flow callee bodies and affected call sites are deliberately declined
extract variable: lambdas and movement across their function/context boundaries are deliberately declined
lambda conversions: require accessible identical signatures; generic inference and unsupported source contexts are declined
coverage: expression bodies count with their enclosing statement; block bodies have ordinary function counters
source inliner and variable extraction: affected lazy expressions and call sites are deliberately declined
cgo: existing restriction on error propagation inside pointer-check rewritten C-call arguments still applies
legacy nil operators provide runtime conveniences; optional guards use the native presence tag; neither adds static non-null guarantees
source inliner declines calls and function bodies containing named arguments until source-order-safe substitution is implemented
initial representation uses a discriminant and separate typed variant storage; no stable layout ABI is promised
checked reflection uses package functions; reflect.Type and Value method sets remain unchanged
unit-only enums use the smallest sufficient tag (up to 256 variants: one byte); enums with payload fields, including zero-size payloads, retain their existing layouts and measured size overhead

ordinary enums require explicit serialization adapters; opt-in string enums supply standard text interfaces, JSON and general database/sql conversions; SQL NULL uses sql.Null[T], pointers or a native optional; native pgx outside database/sql requires a codec; no stable storage ABI is provided
synthesized first-class positional constructors, string parsers and generated string enum methods currently disable compiler inlining
source inlining and extraction across match arms are conservatively declined
variant patterns require qualification; bare payload identifiers bind new variables except contextual true, false and nil; use guards for local constants

enum patterns on interface subjects never prove exhaustiveness (default or case _ is required), do not apply to type-parameter subjects, require the enum value type to implement the interface, and a nil subject matches no enum arm
on interfaces other than error an enum arm is an exact subject.(E) assertion; only predeclared error searches the Unwrap/As tree with errors.AsType semantics
Optional payload extraction is a value operation; presence does not imply a non-nil payload, and a present nil payload keeps ordinary Go nil behavior (gonpls hover explains the distinction)
Optional and legacy nil guards cannot be mixed within one chain; use an explicit payload boundary and preserve nested optionals without automatic flattening
cgo pointer-check rewritten call arguments decline propagation across hidden function boundaries
source inlining and extraction across propagation or lazy operators are conservatively declined
native optional lifting is single-valued and one layer; source transformations decline changes that lose the target context
native optional serialization covers encoding/json (v1 and v2) and database/sql; encoding/xml, gob, other encoders and native pgx outside database/sql need explicit adapters or codecs
optional JSON and SQL reject nested optionals, optional map keys (JSON) and RawBytes payloads (SQL); a present payload that encodes as JSON null is an error
optional equality with untyped nil tests presence without requiring comparable payloads; typed/shadowed nil operands retain ordinary type rules

SQL JSON fallback covers composite optional payloads and ScanStruct composite fields; explicit Scanners retain precedence, raw strings/bytes retain scalar conversions, PostgreSQL array text needs a codec or a JSON query projection
source inlining and extraction decline movement across match arms
source inlining and extraction decline movement across pattern-test scopes and lazy operands
source inlining and extraction decline movement across propagation and implicit error-handler scopes
source inlining and extraction decline moves that change implicit formatting call evaluation or require unavailable import context
nil-flow analysis is opt-in in gon check and gonpls; it does not add non-null types or mandatory compiler diagnostics
external contracts can remain unknown; safe and positive fixtures check specific flows, not general absence of nil panics
upstream NilAway suppresses FldAssign inference without object sensitivity (upstream issue 339); imported constructors with implicit nil fields can lack diagnostics
